header.stage: live with 6 or more complete months of history (12 used)
header.dropped: 2026-10 (incomplete month) and the week of 2026-10-26 (incomplete week); neither is in the test or the baselines
header.baseline_weeks: 2026-09-28 to 2026-10-25 (4 complete Monday-to-Sunday weeks; the week of 2026-09-21 was pulled only to compute the first kept share)

the_pick.north_star: Online bookings completed through the booking page per week, counting every appointment a business's clients book online.
the_pick.why: It is the moment a business gets what it pays for: a client booked without a phone call. Over 10 month pairs, its monthly change lined up with next month's retention change at 0.73 and with next month's revenue change at 0.95, the highest average of the candidates that passed.

candidates.why: Sign-ups rise with ad spend whether or not anyone takes a booking.
A total of every account ever created can't fall, so it can't warn you.
MRR is the result the North Star should predict, so it becomes the revenue series in the test.
The app sends reminders on its own for every booking; more reminders don't mean more value.

candidates.candidate: Share of paying accounts taking online bookings
candidates.why: The share can rise while paying accounts shrink. It stays in view through the booking-account input instead.

candidates.candidate: Accounts with 10 or more online bookings

formulas: bookings per week = booking accounts x booking page visits per booking account x booking conversion
booking accounts this week = booking accounts last week x weekly kept share + accounts starting this week

targets_basis.note: Targets are estimates from this business's own history, not forecasts.

inputs.target_formula: baseline x (1 + median monthly growth of the last 6 complete months)^3 = baseline x (1 + 3.8%)^3
inputs.what_the_owner_changes: Moves only through the inputs below.

inputs.metric: Booking accounts per week (accounts with 1 or more online bookings)
inputs.target_formula: baseline x (1 + 4.9%), the growth the rates don't cover split evenly over the 2 counts
inputs.what_the_owner_changes: Fed by the kept share and the starting accounts.

inputs.metric: Booking page visits per booking account per week
inputs.target_formula: baseline x (1 + 4.9%), the same even split
inputs.what_the_owner_changes: Get each business to share its booking link: Instagram button, Google Business Profile link, email signatures.
inputs.weekly_source: GA4 weekly booking_page_view / BigQuery weekly value_accounts

inputs.metric: Booking conversion (completed bookings / booking page visits)
inputs.target_formula: baseline + half the gap to the best complete month (2026-02, 31.2%)
inputs.what_the_owner_changes: Fewer steps to book, deposits only where the business needs them, clearer time slots.

inputs.metric: Weekly kept share of booking accounts
inputs.target_formula: baseline + half the gap to the best complete month (2026-01, 91.6%)
inputs.what_the_owner_changes: Reach accounts whose bookings stop for a week; check-ins before a quiet season.
inputs.weekly_source: BigQuery weekly query: kept_from_last_week / last week's value_accounts

inputs.metric: Accounts starting to take online bookings per week
inputs.target_formula: N = (BT - B0 x r^13) x (1 - r) / (1 - r^13), with the target kept share
inputs.what_the_owner_changes: Get new accounts to their first online booking: booking page set up and shared in week one.

tracking.calculation: count of booking_completed, Monday to Sunday
tracking.computed_in: GA4 events by date, added up into weeks

tracking.metric: Booking accounts per week (accounts with 1 or more online bookings)
tracking.calculation: accounts with 1 or more booking_completed in the week

tracking.metric: Booking page visits per booking account per week
tracking.computed_in: GA4 weekly count over the BigQuery value_accounts

tracking.metric: Booking conversion (completed bookings / booking page visits)
tracking.computed_in: GA4 events by date, added up into weeks

optional_fields.why: splits visits by the shared link (Instagram button, Google Business Profile, email signature), so Growth marketing can see which link moves visits per account

events.account_id_note: The per-account rows (booking accounts, kept share, starting accounts) count business accounts by user_id, which the product already sets to its internal account id on every event. Keep it that way: never an email address or phone number.
events.key_event_note: booking_completed is already a key event. The weekly check reads event counts, so it doesn't depend on that.

weekly_check.layout: One column per metric; rows for owner, baseline, path at weeks 4 and 8, the week-13 target, then one row per week to fill in each Monday.
weekly_check.status_rule: on track at or above the path. Counts and per-account numbers: watch up to 5% below the path, behind more than 5% below. Rates: watch up to 1 point below the path, behind more than 1 point below.

offered_fix.status: not run (waits for the user's yes on the exact layout)

unknowns_and_caveats: The test covers 10 month pairs, above the 8-pair floor but still a signal, not proof of cause.
December 2025 (the quiet month) and January 2026 (the New Year rebound) move bookings, retention and revenue together for seasonal reasons; they help the correlation without proving the link.
March 2026 (the Instagram booking button launch) lifted bookings; check that retention gains after it hold once the launch effect fades.
Monthly active accounts lined up with next month's retention at 0.24 (weak) and with next month's revenue at 0.13 (none): logging in tracks the business's own activity, not its clients' bookings.
Retention and revenue come from pasted billing history, marked from your data and not checked against the billing system.
go_deeper: onboarding-cro (if installed): raise the share of new accounts that take a first online booking in week one
ab-test-designer (if installed): test a booking-flow change aimed at booking conversion
ltv-cac-ratio-optimizer (if installed): check what a new booking account is worth against what it costs
marketing-plan-builder (if installed): the marketing plan behind the visits-per-account input
